items.stem: Describe three features of plantation agriculture.
items.answer: (1) A single crop is grown on a large area. (2) It needs large capital and migrant labourers. (3) Produce is used as raw material in industries. (4) Examples are tea, coffee, rubber, sugarcane and banana.

items.markingKey: True. In states like Assam, West Bengal and Odisha, three crops of paddy are grown: aus, aman and boro.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a local name for slash and burn agriculture?
items.answer: Bhoodan
items.markingKey: (d) Bhoodan is not a local name for slash and burn agriculture; Milpa, Jhumming, Pamlou are local names for slash and burn agriculture.

items.stem: Define the term 'food security'.
items.answer: Ensuring that all people have access to enough food at all times.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the idea: ensuring that all people have access to enough food at all times.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The White Revolution was also known as Operation Green.
Reason (R): The government announces a minimum support price for important crops to protect farmers from exploitation by speculators and middlemen.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: The White Revolution was also known as Operation Flood. R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
(a) Suggest measures to make Indian agriculture more profitable and sustainable. (3 marks)
(b) Why are Indian farmers finding it hard to compete under globalisation? (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) (1) Diversify from cereals to high-value crops such as fruits, vegetables and flowers. (2) Promote organic farming and efficient irrigation. (3) Improve storage, markets and credit facilities. (4) Use research such as the gene revolution carefully. (b) (1) Farmers in developed countries receive large subsidies. (2) Indian farmers have small holdings and less capital.
items.markingKey: (a) any three points, 1 mark each: (1) Diversify from cereals to high-value crops such as fruits, vegetables and flowers. (2) Promote organic farming and efficient irrigation. (3) Improve storage, markets and credit facilities. (4) Use research such as the gene revolution carefully. (b) any two points, 1 mark each: (1) Farmers in developed countries receive large subsidies. (2) Indian farmers have small holdings and less capital.

items.stem:
Read the revision note prepared by a Class 10 student on "Technological and institutional reforms in agriculture" and answer the questions that follow.
"Vinoba Bhave was offered 80 acres of land by Shri Ram Chandra Reddy at (A) ______. Vinoba Bhave called the Bhoodan-Gramdan movement a (B) ______ revolution."
(i) Fill in blank (A). (1 mark)
(ii) Fill in blank (B). (1 mark)
(iii) Why were institutional reforms in agriculture needed after Independence? (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Pochampalli (ii) bloodless (iii) (1) Small and fragmented landholdings and the zamindari system kept farmers poor. (2) Consolidation of holdings and abolition of zamindari were needed to raise production.
items.markingKey: (i) Pochampalli – 1 mark. (ii) bloodless – 1 mark. (iii) any two points, 1 mark each: (1) Small and fragmented landholdings and the zamindari system kept farmers poor. (2) Consolidation of holdings and abolition of zamindari were needed to raise production.

items.stem: Which of the following correctly describes 'intensive subsistence farming'?
items.answer: Farming in areas of high population with high doses of biochemical inputs and irrigation
items.markingKey: (c) 'Intensive subsistence farming' means farming in areas of high population with high doses of biochemical inputs and irrigation; the other options describe other terms of this chapter.
options: Farming without chemical fertilisers and pesticides, using natural manures
The large increase in food grain production from the use of HYV seeds, fertilisers and irrigation
Farming in areas of high population with high doses of biochemical inputs and irrigation
Combining a farmer's small scattered plots into one compact holding

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Wheat is a rabi crop.
Reason (R): Wheat is sown in winter and harvested in summer.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Define the term 'consolidation of holdings'.
items.answer: Combining a farmer's small scattered plots into one compact holding.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the idea: combining a farmer's small scattered plots into one compact holding.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a kharif crop?
items.answer: Barley
items.markingKey: (d) Barley is not a kharif crop; Jowar, Cotton, Paddy are kharif crops.

items.stem: Name any three local names for slash and burn agriculture.
items.answer: Any three of: jhumming, pamlou, dipa, milpa.
items.markingKey: Any three correct: jhumming, pamlou, dipa, milpa (2 marks for three, 1 mark for two).

items.stem:
Match Column A with Column B and choose the correct option.
Column A:
1. Primitive subsistence farming
2. Horticulture
3. Slash and burn agriculture
4. Golden fibre
Column B:
(p) Farming on small patches of land with primitive tools and family labour, mainly for the family's own needs
(q) The cultivation of fruits and vegetables
(r) A name for jute
(s) Farming in which a patch of forest is cleared and burnt, cultivated for a few years and then left to recover
items.markingKey: (d) Primitive subsistence farming – farming on small patches of land with primitive tools and family labour, mainly for the family's own needs; Horticulture – the cultivation of fruits and vegetables; Slash and burn agriculture – farming in which a patch of forest is cleared and burnt, cultivated for a few years and then left to recover; Golden fibre – a name for jute.

items.stem: State whether the statement is True or False. If false, correct it: The White Revolution was also known as Operation Harvest.
items.answer: False. The White Revolution was also known as Operation Flood.
items.markingKey: False (½ mark); correction: 'Flood' in place of 'Harvest' (½ mark). The White Revolution was also known as Operation Flood.

items.stem:
Read the revision note prepared by a Class 10 student on "Types of farming" and answer the questions that follow.
"Rice is a commercial crop in Punjab and Haryana, but in (A) ______ it is a subsistence crop. Tea plantations are found mainly in Assam and North (B) ______."
(i) Fill in blank (A). (1 mark)
(ii) Fill in blank (B). (1 mark)
(iii) Why is intensive subsistence farming practised in areas of high population? (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Odisha (ii) Bengal (iii) (1) Land holdings are small and the pressure on land is high. (2) Farmers try to get maximum output from limited land using biochemical inputs and irrigation.
items.markingKey: (i) Odisha – 1 mark. (ii) Bengal – 1 mark. (iii) any two points, 1 mark each: (1) Land holdings are small and the pressure on land is high. (2) Farmers try to get maximum output from limited land using biochemical inputs and irrigation.

items.stem: Choose the correct option to complete the statement: Farming without chemical fertilisers and pesticides is called ______ farming.
items.answer: organic
items.markingKey: (b) Farming without chemical fertilisers and pesticides is called organic farming.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a government scheme or reform for farmers?
items.answer: Vernacular Press Act
items.markingKey: (d) Vernacular Press Act is not a government scheme or reform for farmers; Kissan Credit Card, Personal Accident Insurance Scheme, Crop insurance are government schemes and reforms for farmers.

items.stem: On an outline political map of India, locate and label the following: (a) The largest rubber-producing state (b) The largest sugarcane-producing state (c) The largest jute-producing state
items.answer: (a) Kerala – south-west India (b) Uttar Pradesh – north India (c) West Bengal – east India
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct location: (a) Kerala – south-west India (b) Uttar Pradesh – north India (c) West Bengal – east India

items.stem:
Read the revision note prepared by a Class 10 student on "Cropping seasons and major crops" and answer the questions that follow.
"Pulses are leguminous crops that help restore soil fertility by fixing (A) ______ from the air. Arabica coffee, initially brought from Yemen, was first grown in the (B) ______ hills."
(i) Fill in blank (A). (1 mark)
(ii) Fill in blank (B). (1 mark)
(iii) Why are pulses grown in rotation with other crops? (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) nitrogen (ii) Baba Budan (iii) (1) Being leguminous, they fix nitrogen from the air. (2) This restores soil fertility for the next crop.
items.markingKey: (i) nitrogen – 1 mark. (ii) Baba Budan – 1 mark. (iii) any two points, 1 mark each: (1) Being leguminous, they fix nitrogen from the air. (2) This restores soil fertility for the next crop.

items.stem: State whether the statement is True or False. If false, correct it: Arabica coffee, initially brought from Yemen, was first grown in the Nilgiri hills.
items.answer: False. Arabica coffee, initially brought from Yemen, was first grown in the Baba Budan hills.
items.markingKey: False (½ mark); correction: 'Baba Budan' in place of 'Nilgiri' (½ mark). Arabica coffee, initially brought from Yemen, was first grown in the Baba Budan hills.
